# Inkisle

> Inkisle is an offline, single-player island-conquest strategy game for phones, now in development. Send fleets between islands and tint the sea your color. Follow the making, one post a day.

Inkisle is a single-player, offline island-conquest strategy game by ipe() (https://ipe.rest/). It is in development and has NOT been released: no store page, release date or final price exists yet. This site is the game's home and its production journal (one post per day). It has no accounts or ads and collects only basic visit statistics through Google Analytics.

## Key facts

- Real-time island-conquest strategy, single player.
- Stages of about 3 to 5 minutes, played upright with one hand.
- Works offline: no account and no network needed.
- Minimal vector art; each side has its own color and flag shape so it also reads without color.
- Planned for iOS first, with Android developed alongside. No release date yet.

## Pages

- [Home](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/): Inkisle is a quick island-conquest strategy game for your phone. Drag fleets from your islands to the next one: the bigger number takes the island and the ink spreads in your color. Each stage takes a few minutes.
- [About](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/about/): what Inkisle is and who makes it
- [Privacy Policy](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/privacy/)
- [Release notes](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/releases/): what is in each TestFlight build, in plain words
- [Journal](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/): the production journal
- [RSS](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/feed.xml)

## Journal posts (English)

- [Sending from several islands at once: three rewrites of one control](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/three-rewrites-of-multi-island-attack/) — 2026-11-03 — Attacking one island from several of yours was the hardest control in Inkisle. The first drag-based version, the tap-to-select fix and the swipe-to-select version, and what each one taught us.
- [Tuning difficulty with bots: five stages that were wrong](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/tuning-the-difficulty/) — 2026-11-02 — We played every stage with simple bots for 40 seeds each and found stages that were impossible, too short or too hard. The five changes, the win rates before and after, and why bots are not people.
- [A playable prototype in a day](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/a-playable-prototype-in-a-day/) — 2026-11-01 — Sixteen stages, two seas and one HTML file of about 95 KB with no outside requests. How the prototype is built, what we tested in a headless browser, and what we could not test.
- [Art direction: three mockups, one pick](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/art-direction-grace-vs-gpt/) — 2026-10-31 — We asked for the same battle screen from our design assistant (two directions) and from GPT. What each returned, what went wrong with the outside mockup, and why minimal vector won.
- [Naming the game: how we ended up with Inkisle](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/naming-inkisle/) — 2026-10-30 — Ten English name candidates, five finalists, a store and domain check, and why Inkisle won. Including the weak spots we know about and the checks we have not done.
- [The rules on one page: islands, troops, capture](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/the-rules-on-one-page/) — 2026-10-30 — Inkisle's whole rule set on one page: how islands produce troops, how fleets fly, how capture is calculated, and how a match ends. Starting values, before testing.
- [Four game ideas, one core: why we chose island conquest](https://inkisle.ipe.rest/journal/why-island-conquest/) — 2026-10-29 — We drafted four concepts for our next game. All four shared one core, sending troops between nodes. Here is why we kept the core, dropped the story and put it on the sea.

## Languages

The site is available in 12 languages (English and Korean are written by hand, the others are AI translations): English, 한국어, 日本語, 简体中文, Español, Français, Deutsch, Português, Русский, العربية, हिन्दी, Bahasa Indonesia. Each language lives under /<code>/ (English at the root).
